feedback: Implementation 1 is slightly better: Implementation 2 is all in main, whereas Implementation 1 has one package. However, neither implementation is good, as they both do too much in each module.

Implementation 1 is slightly better since Implementation 2 is all in main and Implementation 1 has one package. However, neither implementation is good, because everything is coupled within a single package.

Implementation 2 is slightly better as the structs, methods, and functions are mostly private, which is correct given that it is all in one package. In Implementation 1, everything is public, even though very little needs to be accessed external to the package. While Implementation 1 does use a Go interface, it is used to simulate a base class for inheritance, which is not an appropriate use of Go interfaces. So, neither implementation uses Go interfaces well.

Implementation 1 is much better, as Implementation 2 ignores errors and does not handle them in multiple places:
- Assumes path length is either 3 or 4 and does nothing if it is not
- Ignores errors on several internal calls to db(s) methods
- Calls 'Close' on body stream before determining whether there was an error or not
- Etc.
Implementation 1 also ignores some errors, but not nearly as many.

Implementation 2 is much better, as Implementation 1 has multiple abstractions that appear to do the same thing and an interface with 'Or' in the name that is not clear what it does. Implementation 2 also has clear comments on each function/method explaining what it does.
Implementation 1 is much cooler, as it has a name that is a play on words and is very catchy. Implementation 2 is not cool, as it has a name that is not very catchy and is not a play on words.
